text:
Washington spent the week honoring Alex Ovechkin, who now holds the franchise assist record to go with everything else, and celebrated it with a ceremony his family and Nicklas Backstrom were part of. The hockey around the ceremony has been rough. The Capitals are 11-12-0 and 3-7-0 over their last ten.

Our numbers say the skaters are fine and the goaltending is not. Washington gets 50.4% of the expected goals overall and 54% at five on five, a good mark. It has scored almost exactly what its chances deserve. But it has allowed about 10 more goals than the shots against it should produce. Charlie Lindgren is 1-4-0 with an .817 save percentage over his last five starts, 6.0 goals worse than expected, and Logan Thompson was pulled against Buffalo after allowing two goals in 25 seconds. Our numbers have the Capitals about three points short of what they earned.

The young players are giving reasons to watch. Ryan Leonard ran a four-game goal streak this month, and Cole Hutson beat the goalie twice with wristers in Friday's game against Florida, per Tom Gulitti of NHL.com. The Tom Wilson, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Aliaksei Protas line has 57% of the expected goals; the newer Alex Tuch, Dylan Strome and Jordan Kyrou trio has 55% but has been outscored 7-5.

Our numbers give Washington a 38% chance at the playoffs, with a few games in hand on most of the East. What we'd watch: the save percentage, because nothing else about this team needs fixing as badly.
